subject: On-prem / VPC onboarding — gaps, service accounts, and egress questions
messages:
From: Claire Huang <claire.huang@coralmedical.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
Cc: 
Date: 2025-05-03T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: On-prem kickoff prep + network diagram attached

Hi Aditya,

Thanks again — excited to move forward with the private deployment. Attached is our (very) high-level network diagram and a short list of questions from our infra team:  

1) Egress: we need a concrete list of outbound endpoints/ports that must be allowed (your static IP ranges, telemetry endpoints, model downloads). Can you confirm IPs and whether FQDN allowlisting is supported?
2) Service accounts: we prefer to provision scoped service accounts on our side. Do you have a CSV template for required service-account names/roles and any required key rotation cadence?
3) KMS/HSM: we will be using customer-managed keys in GCP KMS — can you confirm the handshake and required IAM roles?
4) Smoke tests: would you run a staged smoke test (inbound / outbound checks) and provide a runbook for day-0 validation?

Proposed kickoff window: 2025-05-12 to 2025-05-14 (AM PT). Let us know what works.

Attachments: CoralNet_Network_Diagram_v1.pdf

--
Claire Huang
Head of Infrastructure, Coral Medical
claire.huang@coralmedical.com
+1 (415) 555-0198

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@coralmedical.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-03T10:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem kickoff prep + network diagram attached

Claire — thanks for the diagram and the clear questions. Short answers up front, details below and a draft checklist attached.

- Egress: we can provide both IP ranges and FQDNs; best practice is FQDN allowlist for telemetry + model artifacts, IP allowlist for control-plane endpoints. Full list in the attached checklist.
- Service accounts: we prefer customer-provisioned, we have a simple CSV template (attached) with required roles + scopes.
- KMS: GCP KMS handshake is supported; we require a service account with roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter and short-lived binding for the node bootstrap. Exact steps in runbook.
- Smoke tests: yes — we will run a scripted smoke test (connectivity, token verify, sample inference) and share the results.

Attached: Redwood_OnPrem_Onboarding_Checklist_v0.3.pdf, service-account-template.csv

Action items I propose now (owner in parens):
1) Aditya: share day-0 runbook draft by EOD 2025-05-05 (attached draft will be v0).
2) Coral: confirm service-account names + confirm KMS project for key access (Claire).
3) Ben: follow up on reserved capacity windows and procurement delays (Ben).
4) Kimberly: quick security posture review on the attached checklist (Kimberly).

Proposed kickoff: 2025-05-13 09:00 PT (tentative) — if that works we’ll send a calendar invite after a quick dependency check.

Looping in a couple procurement/ops notes from my side — quick bullets:

- Reserved capacity: Coral’s projected baseline throughput (from the PO) maps to one 1.5x reserved pool during business hours; flagging this because it impacts day-0 smoke throughput tests. We should document expected QPS for their simulated traffic in the runbook.
- SLA exceptions: Coral requested a 99.9% SLA on the dedicated pool; we can offer a 99.95% for Dedicated but Private (on-prem) is best-effort — flag with sales/legal if this is a blocker.
- Networking windows: if Coral wants model downloads blocked until we validate, we should include a toggle in the runbook to enable model-sync after smoke pass.

Proposed additional action items:
A) Ben: confirm procurement timeline with Coral (Ben) — assigned.
B) Aditya: include QPS and model-sync toggle in runbook (Aditya).
C) Kimberly: add a short checklist item for audit logging retention + KMS access review (Kimberly).

Reference: HubSpot HB-4521 (Coral Medical) — I’ll open a procurement thread if they confirm the kickoff date.

--
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.ai

From: aditya_rao@redwood.ai
To: Claire Huang <claire.huang@coralmedical.com>
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, kimberly_park@redwood.ai
Date: 2025-05-07T16:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: On-prem kickoff prep + network diagram attached — runbook draft attached

Claire — attaching a short day-0 runbook draft and the checklist we referenced. Summary of changes since our last note:

- Added explicit IP and FQDN tables for control-plane, telemetry, and artifact downloads (Section 2 of checklist).
- Service-account CSV includes exact resource names and IAM roles; we recommend the customer create keys with rotation window 30 days and provide the key resource name for our bootstrap.
- KMS: detailed steps for granting roles/cloudkms.cryptoKeyEncrypterDecrypter to the bootstrap service account and an example IAM binding we will use (Section 4).
- Model-sync toggle: runbook includes a guarded step — model sync remains off until an explicit "GO" from Coral infra after smoke results.
- Smoke tests: three-stage test (network reachability, token/identity validation, sample inference with synthetic payload) plus an automated log bundle we will request for troubleshooting.

Next steps for Coral: please return the filled service-account-template.csv and confirm KMS key resource name by 2025-05-09 so we can finalize the runbook and calendar invite. If the 2025-05-13 kickoff still looks good we’ll hold that slot.

Attachments: Redwood_Runbook_Draft_060525.docx, Redwood_OnPrem_Onboarding_Checklist_v0.3.pdf
